input.rationale: Requests one more revision of the shutdown probe, this time to test the mechanism rather than the symptom. The corrected Fact says the strand comes from a buffered channel whose send stays selectable after the run loop has exited, while Barrier and Apply escape it only because applyCh is unbuffered by default. Config.BatchApplyCh exists precisely to buffer applyCh, and its own comment warns that it breaks the timeout guarantee on Apply, so enabling it should make Barrier and Apply strand exactly like VerifyLeader. The harness now records batch_apply_ch and adds three batched trials each for barrier and apply alongside the default and control cases, with comparisons separating the batched cases from the unbuffered ones. Its execution is requested; no observation is claimed until the receipt exists.

scope.description: Run the shutdown probe for VerifyLeader, Barrier and Apply with the default unbuffered applyCh and again for Barrier and Apply with BatchApplyCh enabled, three trials each, recording how many futures are left incomplete in the racing phase and how many of eight post-shutdown calls are answered in the 500ms window, plus a no-shutdown control.
assumptions: BatchApplyCh is a supported configuration option whose documented effect is to buffer applyCh to MaxAppendEntries and to break the timeout guarantee on Apply.
Buffer size is MaxAppendEntries (the default), which is large enough that the eight post-shutdown sends never block, so the send case is selectable exactly as verifyCh's is.
Single-voter node, in-memory transport, 50ms timeouts, one process, as before.
excluded: BatchApplyCh with BatchApplyChMaxAppendEntries or concurrency large enough to fill the buffer, and multi-node behaviour.

experiment.prefix: Each case starts one real Raft instance with its own InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore and InmemTransport, bootstrapped as a single Voter with HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 50ms and BatchApplyCh set only for the batched cases, and waits until it reports Leader. It emits assurance_shutdown_setup with the batch_apply_ch flag, issues 128 calls of the chosen kind from separate goroutines, each waiting on Error() with a 4000ms deadline, and in the shutdown cases calls Shutdown() from a goroutine 2ms later so the fill and the exit overlap. After Shutdown returns it issues 8 further calls of the same kind one at a time with a 500ms wait each, then emits assurance_shutdown_result with the racing counts, the post-phase counts and histograms, the shutdown error, the node state and the batch_apply_ch flag. The no-shutdown control never calls Shutdown. The harness is TestAssuranceShutdownFutureCompletion.

comparisons.description: Barrier with BatchApplyCh: at least one of eight post-shutdown calls left unanswered, which would show the strand follows the buffering rather than the API.
Apply with BatchApplyCh: same prediction for the documented buffered configuration.
Barrier with the default unbuffered applyCh: every post-shutdown call answered, the contrast that the batched case is measured against.
Apply with the default unbuffered applyCh: same contrast.
VerifyLeader, whose channel is always buffered: the strand re-measured in the same run as the new cases.

experiment.revision_reason: The previous revision isolated the strand to VerifyLeader and attributed it to channel buffering. This revision adds BatchApplyCh cases that buffer applyCh for the Barrier and Apply call kinds, records batch_apply_ch in both events, and adds comparisons for the batched cases against the unbuffered defaults. The existing cases, event names and measured fields are unchanged.

scope.description: Observe VerifyLeader's returned endpoint at the leader of a four-server cluster (three voters plus one non-voter) after partitioning the leader away from the voter majority, comparing a partition that keeps only the non-voter reachable, one that keeps one voter reachable, and one that keeps no peer reachable. Each case emits one CA_EVENT with the leader ID and address, the voters and non-voters read from the leader's latest configuration, the quorum size, the leader term, the other servers' terms and states, the leader's state after the call, the VerifyLeader result and the elapsed time.

basis.prefix: Each case builds four real Raft instances in one process, each with its own InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore and InmemTransport; the transports are fully connected before any node is started. The three voters are bootstrapped with BootstrapCluster from a configuration naming all three as Voter; the fourth node is started without a configuration and joined through the elected leader's own AddNonvoter(id, address, 0, 5s) call, and the case waits until the leader's latest configuration reports the non-voter before proceeding. Configuration: HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 200ms, CommitTimeout = 5ms, default ProtocolVersion, which satisfies Config.Validate. After a 300ms settling period the transports are disconnected in both directions across the chosen boundary, so only the listed peers remain reachable from the leader; the observation then calls VerifyLeader() on the leader and reports nil, a concrete error, or pending after a 900ms wait. The peer kept reachable as a voter is chosen by position in the bootstrap configuration, and the non-voter by its join identity, never by a measured result.

experiments.revision_reason: The previous harness emitted CA_EVENT objects without an event name, so the controller rejected all three as invalid_observation and no observation could be interpreted. This revision only changes the observation format: each case now emits a named assurance_partition_setup event before the partition and a named assurance_verify_leader_result event afterwards, carrying the same measured fields, and declares the setup event as a prerequisite admission with one comparison per partition case.

scope.description: Observe what LeadershipTransferToServer reports against which server actually takes leadership when the requested target is a non-voter, with the same call naming a voter as the only difference. Each case emits an assurance_transfer_target setup event describing the leader, the chosen target, its suffrage in the leader's latest configuration and the voter set, then an assurance_transfer_result event with the returned result, the target's and old leader's states, the leader set and terms after the call, and the time until any leader is observed.
assumptions: Three voters plus one non-voter is a supported configuration; the non-voter is joined through the leader's own AddNonvoter call.
HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 200ms and CommitTimeout = 5ms satisfy Config.Validate; protocol version is the default (>= 3), so LeadershipTransferToServer is supported.
A voter target is a legal and expected use, so the voter case is the control that the probe can observe a real transfer rather than a probe that never succeeds.
excluded: Bounding the length of any leaderless interval: leadership state is sampled at the end of the 1500ms observation window, so this probe does not measure an interval.

basis.prefix: Each case builds four real Raft instances in one process, each with its own InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore and InmemTransport, fully connected before any node starts. Three voters are bootstrapped with BootstrapCluster from a configuration naming them as Voter; the fourth node is started without a configuration and joined through the elected leader's own AddNonvoter(id, address, 0, 5s) call, waiting until the leader's latest configuration reports it. The target is then chosen by configuration role, never by a measured result: in the control case the first voter that is not the leader, in the probe case the joined non-voter; its suffrage is read back from the leader's latest configuration and reported in the setup event. The case calls leader.LeadershipTransferToServer(target.id, target.addr), waits up to 5s for the returned result, then waits up to 1500ms for the requested target to be observed as Leader and separately for any node to be Leader, and finally records the leader set, the maximum term across all four nodes and whether that term rose above the leader's term before the call. Both cases share the harness TestAssuranceLeadershipTransferTarget and are emitted under distinct case names.

Non-voter target: the requested server never became leader within the observation window.
Voter target control: the same call does transfer leadership, so the non-voter outcome is not a probe that never transfers.
Voter target control: the reported result for a transfer that does complete.

scope.description: Observe both halves of a leadership transfer request naming a non-voter: what LeadershipTransferToServer reports, which server actually holds leadership, and how the cluster's leadership state evolves during the attempt, sampled every millisecond, with the same call naming a voter as the control. Each case emits an assurance_transfer_target setup event and an assurance_transfer_result event carrying the returned result, the target and previous-leader states, leader sets and terms, and the sampling counters.
assumptions: Three voters plus one non-voter is a supported configuration; the non-voter is joined through the leader's own AddNonvoter call.
HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 200ms and CommitTimeout = 5ms satisfy Config.Validate, and protocol version >= 3 supports LeadershipTransferToServer.
A voter target is a legal and expected use, so the voter case is the control that the probe can observe a completed transfer.

Sampling every millisecond is fine-grained relative to the 200ms election timeout, so a leaderless interval lasting an election round is expected to be visible; shorter gaps are not bounded by this sampling rate.
excluded: Process-level stalls, host suspends and multi-host clock behaviour, which a single-process in-memory probe does not reproduce.

experiments.revision_reason: The previous run of this harness answered the reported-result half of the question but sampled leadership state only at endpoints, so it could not say whether the cluster was ever without a leader or for how long. This revision adds a 1ms sampling goroutine running from the transfer call until after the observation window, reporting leaderless sample counts, the first and last leaderless millisecond, how often the previous leader was seen outside Leader state, and the endpoint leader identity, with two comparisons asserting those observations for the non-voter case. Measured result fields, cases and target selection are unchanged.

scope.description: Run eight independent trials that each build a three-voter plus one-non-voter cluster, arm a 600ms stall in the leader's log store, partition the leader so that only the non-voter remains reachable, drive a client Apply to block the leader's main loop on that store, queue VerifyLeader during the stall, and report the verify endpoint together with a 1ms leadership sampler over all four servers.
assumptions: The stalling log store models a leader whose disk stalls; StoreLogs then blocks the leader's main loop, which is the goroutine that also serves the lease case and verify requests. The store is a supplied dependency, not a change to production logic.
HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 200ms and CommitTimeout = 5ms satisfy Config.Validate; the stall is 600ms, three times the lease.
Only the elected leader's store is armed, so follower writes and their election timers behave as they would without the stall.
In-memory transports are used in one process, so RPC round trips are much faster than in a networked cluster.
excluded: A leader blocked inside its own lease check rather than inside a store write, and host-level suspensions or clock jumps, which this probe does not reproduce.

basis.prefix: Each trial builds four real Raft instances in one process, each with its own InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore and InmemTransport, fully connected before any node starts; the three voters get a log store that wraps InmemStore and sleeps for 600ms inside StoreLogs while armed, and only the elected leader's store is armed. The three voters are bootstrapped with BootstrapCluster as Voter and the fourth node joins through the leader's own AddNonvoter call, with the trial waiting until the leader's latest configuration reports it. The trial then emits assurance_stall_setup, disconnects the transports in both directions across the partition so that only the leader and the non-voter remain mutually reachable, starts a 1ms sampler that records every server's Leader state and the maximum term, arms the leader's stall, drives one Apply to make the leader write, queues VerifyLeader 300ms later, and reports assurance_stall_trial with the verify endpoint, the sample counters, the term reached, and the stall counters. The harness is TestAssuranceVerifyLeaderDuringLeaderStall.

comparisons.description: The stall was exercised and a different server was observed in Leader state at some point during or after it. Holds means the intended condition was reached.
Conditional on a successor having been observed: whether the queued VerifyLeader still reported success. Holds means the stale-read precondition was witnessed.
Restricted to trials where the stalled leader was never sampled outside Leader state: whether VerifyLeader reported success.

scope.description: Issue 64 VerifyLeader, Barrier or Apply calls in parallel against a freshly started single-voter node while Shutdown runs concurrently, count how many of those futures have not completed 400ms after Shutdown has returned, and compare with the same call kinds issued on a node that is never shut down. Each case emits an assurance_shutdown_setup event and an assurance_shutdown_result event carrying the counts, the outcome histogram and the shutdown error.
assumptions: A single-voter node is a supported configuration and makes each call complete quickly when the node is running, so any incomplete future is attributable to the shutdown race rather than to slow commit.
64 concurrent calls per trial is a probe of exposure, not a rate estimate; the concurrency is what makes the race observable.
Waiting 400ms after Shutdown() has returned is enough for any future that can still be answered, because the run loop has already exited by then.
excluded: Whether a stuck future can be recovered by any other API, and any multi-node variant where a future could still be answered by another goroutine after shutdown.

basis.prefix: Each case starts one real Raft instance in this process with its own InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore and InmemTransport, bootstrapped as a single Voter with HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 50ms, and waits until it reports Leader. The no-shutdown control issues the same calls without ever calling Shutdown. The harness is TestAssuranceShutdownFutureCompletion.

Barrier against a concurrent shutdown: whether the same hang appears on the apply-channel path, which the harness drains in batches.
Apply against a concurrent shutdown: whether the same hang appears for command application.

Each case emits an assurance_shutdown_setup event and an assurance_shutdown_result event carrying the counts, the outcome histograms for both phases and the shutdown error.
assumptions: VerifyLeader is a legal call at any time, including after Shutdown, and the documented generic error for that case is ErrRaftShutdown, which the API's own select returns when the shutdown channel is chosen.
A single-voter node removes commit latency as a confounder and makes every call complete in well under a millisecond while the node is running.
The 4000ms window is long enough that a future answered only by the exited run loop would show as incomplete; nothing else in the harness can answer these futures.
excluded: A BatchApplyCh configuration, where applyCh becomes buffered and the apply path should behave like the verify path; and multi-node variants.

assumptions: VerifyLeader is a legal call at any time, including after Shutdown, and the documented generic error for that case is ErrRaftShutdown, which the API's own select returns when the shutdown channel is chosen.
A single-voter node removes commit latency as a confounder and makes every call complete in well under a millisecond while the node is running.
The 4000ms window is long enough that a future answered only by the exited run loop would show as incomplete; nothing else in the harness can answer these futures.
excluded: A BatchApplyCh configuration, where applyCh becomes buffered and the apply path should behave like the verify path; and multi-node variants.

prefix.before: Each case starts one real Raft instance in this process with its own InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore and InmemTransport, bootstrapped as a single Voter with HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 50ms, and waits until it reports Leader. It then emits assurance_shutdown_setup and issues 64 calls of the chosen kind from separate goroutines, each waiting on Error() with a 1500ms local deadline and recording whether it returned and with which error. Concurrently, in the shutdown cases, Shutdown() is called and the case waits for it to return, then sleeps 400ms so that any future which can still be answered has been, and finally waits for all per-call timers before emitting assurance_shutdown_result with the returned and stuck counts, the outcome histogram, the shutdown error and the node state. The no-shutdown control issues the same calls without ever calling Shutdown. The harness is TestAssuranceShutdownFutureCompletion.
prefix.after: Each case starts one real Raft instance in this process with its own InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore and InmemTransport, bootstrapped as a single Voter with HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 50ms, and waits until it reports Leader. It emits assurance_shutdown_setup, then issues 128 calls of the chosen kind from separate goroutines, each waiting on Error() with a 4000ms deadline and recording whether it returned and with which error. In the shutdown cases a goroutine sleeps 2ms and then calls Shutdown(), so the fill and the exit overlap; the case waits for Shutdown to return, then issues 8 further calls of the same kind one at a time, each waiting 500ms, and records their outcomes; finally it waits for all per-call timers and emits assurance_shutdown_result with the returned, stuck and post-phase counts, the outcome histograms, the shutdown error and the node state. before.description: VerifyLeader against a concurrent shutdown: at least one future never completed. Holds means the predicted hang was observed.

Barrier against a concurrent shutdown: whether the same hang appears on the apply-channel path, which the harness drains in batches.
Apply against a concurrent shutdown: whether the same hang appears for command application.

after.description: VerifyLeader after Shutdown returned: at least one of the eight post-shutdown calls was still unanswered after 500ms. Holds means the predicted strand was observed on a call that has no race with the shutdown itself.
Barrier after Shutdown returned: the contrast case, expected to answer every post-shutdown call with the shutdown error because its channel is unbuffered by default.

result.summary: Requested one more revision of the shutdown probe to test the mechanism rather than the symptom. The corrected Fact attributes the strand to a buffered channel whose send stays selectable after the run loop exits, with Barrier and Apply escaping only because applyCh is unbuffered by default — and Config.BatchApplyCh exists precisely to buffer applyCh, with its own comment warning that it breaks the timeout guarantee on Apply. The harness now records batch_apply_ch and adds three batched trials each for Barrier and Apply beside the default and control cases, with five comparisons separating the batched cases from the unbuffered ones and re-measuring the VerifyLeader strand in the same run. A construction run showed the expected flip — with BatchApplyCh, Barrier answered 5, 5 and 3 of 8 post-shutdown calls and Apply 5, 3 and 5, versus 8 of 8 for both in every unbuffered trial — but no observation is claimed until the clean-copy receipt exists. Unfinished: interpreting that receipt and folding the causal contrast into the account.

scope.description: Observe VerifyLeader's returned endpoint at the leader of a four-server cluster (three voters plus one non-voter) after partitioning the leader away from the voter majority, comparing a partition that keeps only the non-voter reachable, one that keeps one voter reachable, and one that keeps no peer reachable. Each case emits one CA_EVENT with the leader ID and address, the voters and non-voters read from the leader's latest configuration, the quorum size, the leader term, the other servers' terms and states, the leader's state after the call, the VerifyLeader result and the elapsed time.

basis.prefix: Each case builds four real Raft instances in one process, each with its own InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore and InmemTransport; the transports are fully connected before any node is started. The three voters are bootstrapped with BootstrapCluster from a configuration naming all three as Voter; the fourth node is started without a configuration and joined through the elected leader's own AddNonvoter(id, address, 0, 5s) call, and the case waits until the leader's latest configuration reports the non-voter before proceeding. Configuration: HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 200ms, CommitTimeout = 5ms, default ProtocolVersion, which satisfies Config.Validate. After a 300ms settling period the transports are disconnected in both directions across the chosen boundary, so only the listed peers remain reachable from the leader; the observation then calls VerifyLeader() on the leader and reports nil, a concrete error, or pending after a 900ms wait. The peer kept reachable as a voter is chosen by position in the bootstrap configuration, and the non-voter by its join identity, never by a measured result.

scope.description: Observe what LeadershipTransferToServer reports against which server actually takes leadership when the requested target is a non-voter, with the same call naming a voter as the only difference. Each case emits an assurance_transfer_target setup event describing the leader, the chosen target, its suffrage in the leader's latest configuration and the voter set, then an assurance_transfer_result event with the returned result, the target's and old leader's states, the leader set and terms after the call, and the time until any leader is observed.
assumptions: Three voters plus one non-voter is a supported configuration; the non-voter is joined through the leader's own AddNonvoter call.
HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 200ms and CommitTimeout = 5ms satisfy Config.Validate; protocol version is the default (>= 3), so LeadershipTransferToServer is supported.
A voter target is a legal and expected use, so the voter case is the control that the probe can observe a real transfer rather than a probe that never succeeds.
excluded: Bounding the length of any leaderless interval: leadership state is sampled at the end of the 1500ms observation window, so this probe does not measure an interval.

basis.prefix: Each case builds four real Raft instances in one process, each with its own InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore and InmemTransport, fully connected before any node starts. The target is then chosen by configuration role, never by a measured result: in the control case the first voter that is not the leader, in the probe case the joined non-voter; its suffrage is read back from the leader's latest configuration and reported in the setup event. experiments.revision_reason: The previous run of this harness answered the reported-result half of the question but sampled leadership state only at endpoints, so it could not say whether the cluster was ever without a leader or for how long. scope.description: Run eight independent trials that each build a three-voter plus one-non-voter cluster, arm a 600ms stall in the leader's log store, partition the leader so that only the non-voter remains reachable, drive a client Apply to block the leader's main loop on that store, queue VerifyLeader during the stall, and report the verify endpoint together with a 1ms leadership sampler over all four servers.
assumptions: The stalling log store models a leader whose disk stalls; StoreLogs then blocks the leader's main loop, which is the goroutine that also serves the lease case and verify requests. The store is a supplied dependency, not a change to production logic.
HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 200ms and CommitTimeout = 5ms satisfy Config.Validate; the stall is 600ms, three times the lease.
Only the elected leader's store is armed, so follower writes and their election timers behave as they would without the stall.
In-memory transports are used in one process, so RPC round trips are much faster than in a networked cluster.
excluded: A leader blocked inside its own lease check rather than inside a store write, and host-level suspensions or clock jumps, which this probe does not reproduce.

basis.prefix: Each trial builds four real Raft instances in one process, each with its own InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore and InmemTransport, fully connected before any node starts; the three voters get a log store that wraps InmemStore and sleeps for 600ms inside StoreLogs while armed, and only the elected leader's store is armed. The three voters are bootstrapped with BootstrapCluster as Voter and the fourth node joins through the leader's own AddNonvoter call, with the trial waiting until the leader's latest configuration reports it. The trial then emits assurance_stall_setup, disconnects the transports in both directions across the partition so that only the leader and the non-voter remain mutually reachable, starts a 1ms sampler that records every server's Leader state and the maximum term, arms the leader's stall, drives one Apply to make the leader write, queues VerifyLeader 300ms later, and reports assurance_stall_trial with the verify endpoint, the sample counters, the term reached, and the stall counters. The harness is TestAssuranceVerifyLeaderDuringLeaderStall.

comparisons.description: The stall was exercised and a different server was observed in Leader state at some point during or after it. Holds means the intended condition was reached.
Conditional on a successor having been observed: whether the queued VerifyLeader still reported success. Holds means the stale-read precondition was witnessed.
Restricted to trials where the stalled leader was never sampled outside Leader state: whether VerifyLeader reported success.

scope.description: Issue 64 VerifyLeader, Barrier or Apply calls in parallel against a freshly started single-voter node while Shutdown runs concurrently, count how many of those futures have not completed 400ms after Shutdown has returned, and compare with the same call kinds issued on a node that is never shut down. Waiting 400ms after Shutdown() has returned is enough for any future that can still be answered, because the run loop has already exited by then.
excluded: Whether a stuck future can be recovered by any other API, and any multi-node variant where a future could still be answered by another goroutine after shutdown.
